newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH SKODA CHAIRMAN SAYS HAS STATE STAKE INTEREST.
newsitem.headline: CZECH SKODA CHAIRMAN SAYS HAS STATE STAKE INTEREST.

text.p: Lubomir Soudek, chairman and the largest shareholder of Czech engineering concern Skoda a.s. , said he is interested in buying the state's 8.7 percent stake.

Speaking to reporters at a business forum in Prague, Soudek said he opposed a plan presented by the state privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (NPF), to sell the shares on the capital market.
"We of course have interest in the NPF stake, together with (banks) Komercni Banka a.s. and IPB a.s. ," he said.

"We would like to keep the eight percent in this consortium and we would not like it to be taken out. It would only destabilise the company. To sell it on the capital market would not be a serious approach of the NPF," he added.

Soudek's firm NERo s.r.o. holds 21.5 percent in the company, based in the western Czech city of Plzen. Komercni Banka, along with its investment funds holds about 12 percent of Skoda, while IPB has roughly six percent.

Soudek also said he was not pleased that Slovak steel mill VSZ a.s. has expressed an interest in possibly taking an unspecified stake in the company, but added that while he had not been been contacted by VSZ, he also could not stop it from acquiring Skoda shares.
"We cannot avoid (VSZ buying into Skoda) if they buy from other shareholders. We do normally cooperate with VSZ, but I see no reason why they should enter Skoda," he said.
Skoda's production range spreads from beer cans to trucks and nuclear reactors. It is no longer affiliated with Volkswagen AG's Czech unit, car maker Skoda Automobilova a.s..
